changes.after: A fiber is a piece of work that can pause and let its caller take a turn.

before: Fiber receives a callback. start begins it and returns the value passed to Fiber::suspend; resume continues execution and supplies a value back to that suspension point. This is explicit cooperative control transfer, not parallel execution.

After the callback terminates, getReturn obtains its return value. resume itself does not return that final callback value in this example. Fibers do not make blocking file or network calls nonblocking and do not install an asynchronous runtime automatically.

Expected output or behavior: paused
done:ok. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
